subject: Stratify PoC message contract and SDK/auth questions
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@stratify.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stratifiy PoC message contract and SDK/auth questions

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on the PoC goals. Per our notes, I'm sending a concise post-call recap and a set of integration questions that will help us spin up a working PoC quickly (we attached the proto schema and a couple sample payloads). Please answer the numbered items below or tell us who on your side should own each.

Recap (short):
- PoC scope: 1) live request/response for customer support triage (chat + rerank) 2) embeddings for similarity search, 3) structured tool-calling for ticket creation.
- Target QPS: 5-10 sustained, spikes to ~50 for specific campaigns.
- Latency requirement: p95 < 250ms for inference-only path; end-to-end SLA is relaxed for the PoC.

Please confirm the following so we can prepare an environment and a skeleton integration: 

1) SDK language and onboarding: which language will you use for your app? We can provide a Python and a Node quickstart — let us know preference.

2) Auth and credentials: do you want to use static API keys for the PoC, or can you accept temporary service account tokens (recommended if you want scoped access & rotation)? Any restriction on outbound mTLS?

3) Routing policy: do you want all traffic to go to Redwood-hosted models initially, or do you need region affinity / private deployment? If routing by priority matters (cost vs latency), state suggested weights.

4) Structured output / tool calling: our runtime supports function-style tool calling (JSON schema enforcement). For ticket creation, do you want the model to return a strict JSON payload (schema attached) or free-form then a separate parse step? Also: will your ticketing API accept the exact schema or do we need an adaptor?

5) Embeddings + rerank: do you expect a two-stage pipeline (embed -> ANN -> cross-encoder rerank) or a simple embed-only retrieval? If a reranker is required, where do you prefer it hosted (your side vs Redwood)?

6) Request/response contract: a) chat vs completions — which mode better matches your UX for triage? b) token budget concerns: max_tokens for responses, stop tokens you rely on, and whether you need streaming for partial suggestions.

7) Edge cases / tokenization: we recommend validating client-side tokenization (we use a variant compatible with tiktoken) before sending large contexts. Any long documents (>20k tokens) we should pre-process?

Next steps: If you can reply with answers to 1-6 and a preferred time for a short PoC kickoff (30-45m) later this week, we'll provision a sandbox team API key and push a skeleton repo to your Drive.

Attachments: stratify_mvp_schema.proto (message schemas), sample_payloads.json (sample requests/responses), redwood_sla_notes.pdf (PoC SLA notes)

Thanks,
Irene

From: Daniel Park <daniel@stratify.ai>

Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stratifiy PoC message contract and SDK/auth questions

Great recap — thanks Irene. Short answers below to keep momentum; happy to loop in our infra lead if you need deeper detail.

1) SDK language: primary app is Node (backend microservice), but we have a Python infra script for data ingest. Node quickstart would be ideal.

2) Auth: for the PoC we prefer temporary service tokens (rotated) — avoids leaking long-lived keys. Outbound mTLS is not available from our staging environment today.

3) Routing: start with Redwood-hosted models in us-west; we may want region affinity later but not for PoC. Cost vs latency: prefer p95 latency, so route to faster variants with higher weight.

4) Structured output: prefer strict JSON schema for ticket creation (we can adapt on our side if minor mismatches appear). We'll accept the schema you attached; we can confirm exact field mapping after seeing sample outputs.

5) Embeddings/rerank: we want a two-stage pipeline: embed -> ANN -> cross-encoder rerank. Prefer the reranker to run on Redwood side initially if you recommend it; otherwise we can host a simple cross-encoder in our infra.

6a) UX mode: chat mode maps better to triage (multi-turn context). 6b) Token budget: start conservative — max_tokens=256 for responses; stop tokens: ["\nTicket:"] (we'll test). Streaming: yes, would like partial suggestions to show in the UI.

7) Tokenization: we'll pre-split >10k tokens. No massive docs in the PoC.

We'll take the Node quickstart. For the PoC kickoff slot, Thurs 18 Apr 10:00 PT works. I'll also share a short infra contact (cc'd platform@stratify.ai) who can accept a scoped service token.

--Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Product Engineering | Stratify AI
daniel@stratify.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@stratify.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2028 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stratifiy PoC message contract and SDK/auth questions

Thanks Daniel — helpful. A few implementation clarifications and recommended defaults from our side so the PoC is low friction: 

- SDK quickstart: we'll push a Node repo with examples for chat, embeddings, and rerank wiring. The chat example will show the structured tool-calling path (we'll include a sample function signature).

- Auth: we'll issue short-lived JWT service tokens for the PoC (30d), delivered via a secure share. These tokens are bearer tokens and scoped to the PoC project. No mTLS required on our side for PoC.

- Routing & model choices: recommend using our 'rwd-fast-chat-1' for chat (lower latency, higher cost) and 'rwd-embed-2' for embeddings. We'll set routing to prefer rwd-fast-chat-1 with a 90/10 weight that falls back to a cheaper baseline if warm capacity is not available. We can tweak after initial runs.

- Structured tool-calling: we'll implement the ticket-create function as strict JSON. Important implementation note: when using streaming with function responses, the runtime emits incremental chunks of the function args payload as events — the final event contains a complete JSON. Our client helper will reassemble. If your UI wants interim partial fields, we can expose them, but be aware incomplete JSON until stream end.

- Streaming semantics & stop tokens: streaming uses SSE-like chunked events. Stop tokens are enforced by the model decode but in streaming you may still see trailing tokens if the model emits before the stop is recognized; clients should treat the stream as authoritative and rely on the final event for schema-validated outputs. For UI partials, truncate safely and avoid displaying until a delimiter.

- Tokenization & max_tokens: Redwood enforces max_tokens at decode time; however, long prompts should be truncated client-side to avoid wasted compute. We recommend the client compute an estimated token count (we'll provide a token-counter utility in the repo). For PoC defaults: max_context_tokens=8192, max_response_tokens=256.

- Embeddings & rerank: we'll offer a hosted reranker (cross-encoder) as a managed option for the PoC. Latency estimate: rerank add ~80-160ms per query depending on candidate set size. For 5-10 QPS this is within your p95 target if we cap reranker candidates to 20. We'll include a config example.

Next steps from our side:
1) I'll create the Node quickstart repo and share a drive link by EOD today.
2) Irene will provision a scoped service token and upload to the shared drive.
3) Schedule kickoff Thu 18 Apr 10:00 PT (Irene, Ben, Laura, Daniel + infra contact).

If that matches, we'll lock and I can start wiring the rerank endpoint in the sandbox.

Ben
